description:
Independent of protocol dispatch (fz-9i4.7.2/fz-bin). On a list-only program (which COMPILES, no multi-target error), Enum.take/drop return empty lists:

  Enum.take([1,2,3], 5) -> []   (expect [1,2,3])
  Enum.take([1,2,3], 2) -> []   (expect [1,2])
  Enum.drop([1,2,3], 1) -> []   (expect [2,3])

But on the same path:
  Enum.reduce([1,2,3], 0, fn(x,a)->x+a end) -> 6   (correct)
  Enum.map([1,2,3], fn(x)->x*2 end) -> [2,4,6]      (correct)

So reduce and map (full-fold list build) are correct; take/drop (which fold with an early {:halt, acc} and a tuple/count accumulator, then extract+reverse) return empty. Likely a bug in the halt/cont accumulator extraction or the {count,list}->list unwrap/reverse in Enum.take/drop (runtime_library/enum.fz), OR in how the halting reduce's {:halted, acc} result is unwrapped. Repro: fixtures2/00420_enum_take_drop_split.fz once it compiles (needs fz-bin), or the one-liners above. This blocks enum_take_drop_split producing correct output independent of the dispatch fix. Investigate the take/drop reduce-halt path; verify against the oracle in fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.expected.txt.
title: [BUG] Enum.take/drop/split return [] even when monomorphic (compile OK)
